subject.title: bug(agents): nodes tool describe action fails with 'node required' due to schema/implementation mismatch

question: For omitted-node `nodes` `describe`, should OpenClaw default to the current/default node, return list-style discovery output, or combine single-node defaulting with multi-node listing?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the issue discussion and open PR propose different valid semantics for discovery in multi-node setups, so automation should not choose the permanent behavior contract alone.

options.title: Default to current node
options.body: Accept the open PR direction after adding proof and regression coverage, making omitted-node `describe` use the existing default-node resolver.

options.title: Return discovery list
options.body: Replace the open PR with a patch where omitted-node `describe` returns node list data instead of selecting a target node.

options.title: Hybrid behavior
options.body: Default when there is a single obvious node and return list-style output when multiple candidates would make implicit targeting ambiguous.

recommendation.title: Default to current node
recommendation.body: Accept the open PR direction after adding proof and regression coverage, making omitted-node `describe` use the existing default-node resolver.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent and historical ownership signal across the nodes tool schema, runtime, and resolver surfaces.
